_comment: Phase 1 winner-pursuit verification (docs/far-tier-pursuit-contagion-design.md; see that file's 'Phase 1 as verified' section for the full account). A lone far-tier Cavalry regiment (team 1, the whole AI roster -- Subcommander.decide_group short-circuits to {} for a group under 2 living members, so UnitLeader.decide's own nearest-enemy fallback runs unshadowed by any hold-line/cover-flank directive) starts nearest a weakened far-tier Spearmen formation (team 0, non-ranged so the cavalry takes no free hits while closing) and engages it through FarTierCombat (phase 0). The Spearmen enter ROUTING at tick 165 but keep taking casualties while fleeing (fleeing grants no immunity) and die -- not merely rout -- by tick 207: UnitTargeting.current_target only clears target_enemy on DEAD, so the rout itself never unlocks the retarget, only the death does. Thirty-four ticks later (the wait is Battle.AI_PERIOD = 60: the prior AI decision ran at tick 180 while the Spearmen were still alive, the next lands at tick 240, first visible in the tick-241 dump), the cavalry's target_enemy_uid flips straight to a second, undamaged Infantry formation positioned close enough to become the nearer target once the Spearmen are gone. promote_range is 0 (as in the phase-0 demo): the tier pass measures the gap between the blocks' edges, which is exactly 0 once two blocks are in contact, so no positive promote range can hold a melee fight at the far tier, and the demote range is 20 wu so the opening edge gaps (the Cavalry squadron is 3 ranks deep, so it starts 890 - 730 = 160 wu from the Spearmen but only about 30 wu clear of them) still collapse all three to the far tier. The Infantry stand 170 wu behind the Spearmen on the flight side, far enough that the rout does not take them with it; measured, both formations stay far-tier for the whole clip -- including the cavalry's second fight against the Infantry -- so this scenario demonstrates the 'fighting it (Phase 0)' branch of the phase-1 done-check rather than the promotion branch. Frontages are kept modest (not single-rank) after an earlier attempt with a 30-wide single-rank cavalry line produced a facing whipsaw while pivoting toward the new target (Lacaedemon/sparta#1616) -- a staging artifact of that extreme aspect ratio, not a defect in the retarget logic itself. Every tick number in this comment (and in state/frames/expect below) is on the 60 Hz dump-state.sh basis; camera keyframes below are authored on demo.621.json's fixed_fps (30) basis instead, per demos/README.md's 'camera/max_frames and state/frames ticks live on two different tick bases' note -- a camera tick is roughly half the 60 Hz tick it is meant to frame.
